AgentCreate.description: A new agent: the agent spec itself. Unknown keys (hosts, egress) are refused.
AgentCreate.title: AgentCreate

AgentUpdate.description:
Changes to a person's agent, made against ``expected_revision``.
Keys left out keep their value; ``slug`` cannot change.
AgentUpdate.title: AgentUpdate

ArtifactPage.description:
A run's catalog, and — separately — where the run published: a
catalog entry is a file on the host, a ``published`` entry a sink
that took it.
ArtifactPage.title: ArtifactPage

ArtifactRefOut.description:
A file a run delivered, by catalog identity; its bytes are served by
``GET /v1/artifacts/{id}``.
ArtifactRefOut.title: ArtifactRefOut

AuthorOut.description: Who wrote a message: a person, an agent, or sbxloop itself.
AuthorOut.title: AuthorOut

BridgeOut.description: A chat service this release can bridge, and whether it is set up.
BridgeOut.title: BridgeOut

ChannelArtifactPage.description: Every file a channel's messages carry.
ChannelArtifactPage.title: ChannelArtifactPage

ChannelLinkCreate.description:
Link a surface of a chat service to this channel.

``allow_guests`` admits people on that surface who have linked no
account: their messages are stored under the name they use there.
ChannelLinkCreate.title: ChannelLinkCreate

ChannelParticipantOut.description:
An agent in a channel. ``status`` is ``thinking`` while it answers a
running turn here, ``working`` while a live run in this channel is
credited to it, and ``idle`` otherwise; ``activity`` names that run.
ChannelParticipantOut.title: ChannelParticipantOut

ChannelParticipantUpdate.description: Only the fields sent change; a new participant answers when mentioned.
ChannelParticipantUpdate.title: ChannelParticipantUpdate

ChannelUpdate.description:
Only the fields sent change. Changing either one takes managing the
channel: its owner, or a workspace owner or admin.
ChannelUpdate.title: ChannelUpdate

Configuration.description:
The allowlisted effective configuration: never a secret value,
never a host path; ``sections`` says what is readable at all.
Configuration.title: Configuration

DaemonCommandResult.description:
A stop or restart accepted: the effect follows the reply, so a
client that sees this body has a durable record, not a process exit.
DaemonCommandResult.title: DaemonCommandResult

EventOut.description:
One public event. ``id`` is the replay cursor (``evt_<seq>``);
``native_seq`` is the engine's own sequence when the event is a
projection of the run's chronology; ``actor`` is absent where nothing
truthful can be said.
EventOut.title: EventOut

LinkCodeOut.description: A code to type on a bridge, once, to prove an account is yours.
LinkCodeOut.title: LinkCodeOut

LogTail.description: The daemon's most recent log records, oldest first, redacted.
LogTail.title: LogTail

MessageOriginOut.description: The bridge surface a message arrived on, for a message that did.
MessageOriginOut.title: MessageOriginOut

OidcProviderOut.description: What a signed-out browser needs to start Authorization Code + PKCE.
OidcProviderOut.title: OidcProviderOut

OidcTokenRequest.description: The browser's authorization code, redeemed by the daemon.
OidcTokenRequest.title: OidcTokenRequest

Origin.description:
Where a work item came from. ``ref`` is the id the daemon's own
surfaces (ctl, chat, the console) know the item by.
Origin.title: Origin

ParticipantOut.description:
One agent's slot in a turn. ``assignees`` is set on the first slot of
a turn that may start managed work: the run roles the turn's mentions
declare, as ``role -> agent slug``, which admission uses to assign the
run.
ParticipantOut.title: ParticipantOut

QueuePage.description: The queue in dispatch order, with what stands in its way.
QueuePage.title: QueuePage

ScheduleUpdate.description: Complete replacement for one schedule, applied atomically.
ScheduleUpdate.title: ScheduleUpdate

Status.description: The daemon's live state, observed at ``observed_at``.
Status.title: Status

UsagePool.description:
Today's workspace budget pool: runs against the daily cap and
reported tokens (input plus output) against the daily budget, for the
calendar day in ``[daemon] run_cap_timezone``.
UsagePool.title: UsagePool

WorkspaceInviteCreated.description: A new invite. ``token`` appears here and nowhere else.
WorkspaceInviteCreated.title: WorkspaceInviteCreated

WorkspaceUserOut.description: One person in the workspace directory.
WorkspaceUserOut.title: WorkspaceUserOut

get.description: The API process answers; it says nothing about execution.
Recovery has established execution ownership and commands are taken.

The agents a client shows. ``include_disabled`` (for clients that may
edit agents, ``collaboration:write``) adds disabled and archived agents
and the legacy built-in names, so an agent switched off can be found and
switched back on.

schema.title: Response List Agents V1 Agents Get
Response List Memories V1 Agents  Slug  Memories Get

get.description: Digest, media type, size, origin and availability.

The bytes, as an attachment: never rendered, never a path the
client chose, opened relative to the run's own directory without
following a link out of it. ``410`` once the run was pruned.

post.description:
Redeem an OpenID Connect authorization code (Authorization Code +
PKCE, run by the browser) for a token pair. The daemon authenticates to
the provider as the confidential client, validates the ID token, and
creates the account on a first sign-in. Needs no token.

get.description:
The sign-ins a signed-out client may offer. Needs no token. ``oidc``
is null unless a provider is configured and its discovery answered.

post.description:
End this access token now (it would otherwise run to its expiry),
and a refresh token's whole family when one is named.

Exchange client credentials, or a refresh token, for a token pair.
A refresh token is single-use: presenting one twice revokes its
family, and the client authenticates with its secret again.

get.description:
The chat services a channel can be linked to, and whether this daemon
has one set up. An unconfigured service can still be linked: the link
starts working when the operator configures the bridge.

Every file this channel's messages carry, newest message first.

Channel read permission, not ``artifacts:read``: a file delivered into
a conversation belongs to the people in it. ``GET /v1/runs/{id}/artifacts``
is unchanged and still takes ``artifacts:read``.

The bytes of one of the channel's files, as an attachment.

Resolved through the channel: a file this channel does not carry is
``404`` whatever else the caller may read, so an id from elsewhere
never leaks through here.
The bridge surfaces mirroring this channel; takes managing it.

post.description:
Mirror a bridge surface into this channel; takes managing it and a
workspace owner or admin. A surface carries one link, so a second one
is refused, and a run's thread cannot be linked.

Add a workspace member to the channel (201); takes managing the
channel. An explicit ``role`` for a current member with another role
changes it in place (200).

delete.description:
Remove someone from the channel (managing it), or leave it (one's own
id). The last owner cannot leave while anyone else remains.

schema.title: Response List Messages V1 Channels  Channel Id  Messages Get

put.description: Add an agent to the channel, or change how it takes part.

schema.title: Response List Turns V1 Channels  Channel Id  Turns Get
Response Channel Work V1 Channels  Channel Id  Work Get

get.description:
The configuration this daemon runs on, restricted to the sections a
remote operator may read, with the layer each key comes from, whether
a change applies live, whether the file on disk now says otherwise,
and what keeps the daemon's own tools from changing it. Never a secret
value, never a host path; the listener's own settings are not here.

schema.title: Response List Connections V1 Connections Get
Response Connection Services V1 Connections Services Get

get.description:
Every hold standing, with whose it is and why: while any stands
nothing new is claimed; the run in flight is not touched.

post.description:
Take a named hold attributed to this client. It persists across a
restart and is never released by a disconnect: release it, or let an
operator override it. ``201`` for a new hold, ``200`` for one already
standing under that name.

delete.description:
Release one hold. Another principal's is refused as
``409 hold_owned`` unless ``force=true`` says this is an override,
which the operation records as such.

post.description:
A stop the supervisor undoes: refused as ``409 unsupervised`` when
nothing would start the daemon again. ``now`` cancels the run in
flight first (it is resumable). The reply carries the generation that
accepted the request; the daemon is back when ``/health/ready``
reports a new one.

Ask the daemon to stop gracefully: nothing new is claimed, the run
and landing in flight finish, then the process exits — and this
listener with it. ``202`` is durable acceptance, not the exit: a
stream hears ``daemon.stop_requested``, then ``closing``; a poll of the
operation may find the connection refused. Under a service manager
that restarts the daemon this is a restart, and every hold standing
now still stands when it is back.

get.description:
Every public event after ``after`` (an event id, or omitted for
the oldest held), oldest first, in the order it was recorded.
``latest`` instead returns the newest bounded snapshot, oldest first;
it works after retention and cannot be combined with ``after``.
``channel_id`` narrows to one channel's events (and its runs'). A
workspace member sees only what they may: see ``events.scoped``.

Server-sent events from the same durable cursor space. Resume with
``Last-Event-ID`` (or ``after``); each frame's ``id`` is the cursor
to resume from. Pings are comments. The stream closes when the daemon
stops or the token is revoked; reconnect with the last id seen.
Outstanding and resolved merge and publication gates, newest first.
The gate's revision, subject, required authority and available actions.

post.description:
Endorse and release the gate at exactly the revision the person
saw (``expected_revision`` is required; a moved gate is
``409 stale_revision``, a second approval ``409 already_in_progress``).
Success is the recorded approval and the committed release; the merge
or publication completes afterwards and is a separate event.

get.description: Work items, newest first, filterable by state, kind and repository.

post.description:
Admit work through its source's rules: an existing issue in a
configured repository (labelled as a person would, so polling
converges on the same item), an inline workload under an allowed
profile, or a registered tool recipe with validated parameters. An
``Idempotency-Key`` is required; a replay answers with the same item
and operation. ``201`` when the item was created, ``200`` when it was
already queued.

get.description: The request, its origin, its state, and every run it had.

post.description:
Give the item up with an attributed reason; the source hears the
ordinary abandon report.

Unpin the item's run so its next dispatch starts fresh, attempts
intact; the run in flight is cancelled.

A fresh attempt for a settled item: attempts reset, the run
unpinned, the source told who asked.

get.description:
The most recent records of the daemon's in-process log ring —
at most ``LOG_TAIL_MAX`` — at or above ``level``, containing ``grep``
(a plain substring, never a pattern); credential-shaped text is
masked before it leaves the host.
The authenticated client and the capabilities its token carries now.
Recent operations, newest first, filterable by state and target.
The ``[[workloads]]`` profiles an inline workload may be admitted under.

schema.title: Response List Preferences V1 Prompts Get
Response Preference Definitions V1 Prompts Definitions Get

get.description:
The queue in the order dispatch considers it — interrupted runs
awaiting resume first, then oldest first — with each entry's own
eligibility and what holds the whole queue.
The registered tool recipes and the parameters each takes.
Every configured repository with its polling health.

post.description:
Poll a suspended or backing-off repository again now; one that is
polling normally is refused by name.

get.description: Runs touched most recently first, filterable by state and kind.
The run's summary, stage, result, gate and available actions.
The run's catalog, and separately where the run published.

post.description:
Cancel this run wherever the daemon holds it — never another run
that happens to be current. A run in flight stops at its next
boundary (``202``: the operation finishes when it does); a parked one
is settled now. ``expected_revision`` refuses a cancel meant for an
earlier state.

get.description:
The run's chronology after a cursor: its own engine events, and the
daemon's notices and transitions that name it.

post.description:
Admit a persisted run to the daemon's own queue for resume: the
next tick continues it through the same gates a fresh dispatch faces.
Never a second engine.

Re-arm the wait for an external review and check the pull request
now; the review itself stays a person's on the forge.

Grant a run that exhausted its fix rounds a bounded number more,
and re-admit it on its own pull request.

get.description:
Every instruction submitted to the run, oldest first, with its
delivery and handling status.

post.description:
Submit explicit direction to the run in flight. Acceptance means
the instruction was durably handed to the run's input path; the
agent's reply and any course change follow on the record and in the
chronology. Refused for a run that is not in flight or a tool run.

get.description: The task graph with each task's progress and verification summary.

schema.title: Response Get Tasks V1 Runs  Run Id  Tasks Get

get.description:
Tokens and turns the run's backend reported, by persona and by
phase and model; unknown values stay unknown.
Every schedule with its cadence, last due, next due and who paused it.

post.description:
Create a schedule under the rules the concierge's tool applies: a
declared profile, a free name, exactly one cadence. Live from the
next tick.

delete.description: Delete the schedule and its state; a tick already queued or running is untouched.

patch.description: Atomically replace a schedule while preserving its pause and firing history.

post.description: Park the schedule: its ticks are swallowed until it is resumed.
Release a parked schedule; a tick that passed while paused is not made up.

get.description:
Live current/claiming state, queue counts, holds, breaker, stopping,
version and the time it was observed. Live, not a database snapshot:
an unavailable daemon answers 503 rather than a stale picture.

schema.title: Response List Teams V1 Teams Get

get.description:
Reported usage across the runs touched in a window (RFC 3339 or
epoch bounds; the daemon's current calendar day when omitted; at most
90 days wide).

Today's workspace budget pool: runs against `[daemon]
max_runs_per_day` and reported input plus output tokens, from runs and
chat turns, against `[daemon] daily_token_budget`.
Everyone in the workspace, active or not, oldest member first.

post.description:
A code to type on a bridge, as ``!sbx link <code>``, so messages you
send on a linked surface post under this account. It is single use and
short-lived, and this is the only place it is shown.

delete.description:
Forget who this account is on a bridge. Messages already stored keep
the author they were written with.

schema.title: Response List Workflows V1 Workflows Get

get.description: Pending and spent invites, newest first, without their tokens.

post.description:
A new invite. Its token is in this response only; the daemon keeps a
hash.

delete.description: Withdraw an unspent invite; its token admits nobody afterwards.

End a membership: the user's client keeps no capability and its
refresh tokens are revoked in the same transaction.

patch.description:
Change a member's role or deactivate (or reactivate) them. A
deactivated user's tokens stop working and their refresh tokens are
revoked in the same transaction as the change.
